subject: MAP milestones and escrowed credits — uplift & renewal schedule
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@novagrid.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novagrid.ai
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial MAP draft + ask on escrowed credits

Markus —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. The team at NovaGrid is excited about Redwood’s latency profile and the cost controls you showed. We’re starting to draft an internal MAP so procurement can sign off, but we have two key asks we need clarified before we proceed:

1) Escrowed credits: procurement wants a mechanism where a portion of committed credits is escrowed and released on milestone acceptance (pooled across environments). Can you confirm Redwood offers this or a third-party escrow option?

2) Renewal uplift: Leadership wants comfort that the renewal uplift will be limited if we hit the MAP milestones (we can’t accept open-ended increases tied to usage growth). Can you outline typical uplift bands (if any) and how they map to commit/ramp?

Attached: NovaGrid_MAP_draft_v1.pdf (MAP draft, internal)

Goal: Get a mutual action plan we can share with procurement/legal by end of next week.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Torres
VP, Platform & Ops
NovaGrid

From: markus.klein@redwood.com <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@novagrid.ai>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MAP draft + ask on escrowed credits

Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks — both are reasonable and we can structure the MAP to address them. High-level proposal below (happy to convert into a revised MAP PDF):

- Escrowed credits: We support an escrow model via a neutral custodian or by Redwood holding a flagged balance in the contract that’s only released on signed milestone acceptance. Typical split: 20% held in escrow at contract start, released across 3 acceptance milestones (initial eval sign-off, performance ramp to X TPS, final production roll). We’ll share standard escrow terms for your legal review.

- Renewal uplift bands: We can cap uplift linked to baseline committed units. Example structure: if NovaGrid meets MAP milestones and achieves the committed ramp, renewal uplift is capped at +5% YoY for the subsequent 12 months. If milestones are missed, uplift band expands to +15% (or customer can renegotiate with notice). We can also lock pricing for specific model classes.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) I’ll prepare Redwood_MAP_Proposal_v2 (with milestone schedule, escrow clause, and uplift caps).
2) Can we get a short call with procurement/legal next week (30 min) to walk the proposal and identify redlines?
3) If acceptable, we’ll route the MAP to DocuSign with escrow terms attached.

I’ve looped in Lauren (deals) to confirm recommended commit sizes and Rishi (pricing) to validate uplift bands against the deal economics.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@novagrid.ai>, procurement@novagrid.ai
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Initial MAP draft + ask on escrowed credits

Markus / Rishi —

Quick internal notes before the call:

- Recommended commit profile for NovaGrid (based on their usage pattern): 500k tokens/month for Q1, 1.5M tokens/month by month 6, 3M tokens/month by month 12. We’d surface a 10% discount at the 1.5M threshold and a stretched discount (15%) at 3M if customer signs a 12-month committed term.

- Escrow mechanics: Legal prefers the ‘‘flagged balance’’ approach (Redwood escrow accounting entry + release triggers) rather than a third-party custodian for speed. We’ll provide a boilerplate escrow_term.docx for procurement.

- Renewal uplift recommendation: tie capped uplift to MAP milestone completion. If they complete 75%+ of milestones, cap at +5%; 50-75% cap at +10%; <50% open to negotiation (but we want to avoid >+15% automatic increases). Rishi — confirm these bands are financially palatable.

I’ll join the call and own post-signing onboarding checkpoints.

-Lauren
Director, Deals — Redwood Inference

From: Elena Torres <elena@novagrid.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novagrid.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MAP draft + ask on escrowed credits

Markus / Lauren —

Thanks for the proposed structure; that approach is promising. A few clarifying points from procurement and FP&A after internal review:

- Escrow amount: procurement prefers 25% rather than 20% given initial unknowns. Can Redwood accept 25% held in escrow across 3 milestones with the same release triggers?

- Milestone acceptance criteria: we need objective, measurable criteria (SLO numbers, latency percentiles, and ramp thresholds). The MAP draft should include exact metrics for each milestone.

- Renewal uplift lock: FP&A requests that the +5% cap only applies if both (a) MAP milestones achieved, and (b) average monthly spend across months 10–12 meets the committed levels. Otherwise, the +10% band applies.

Attached: NovaGrid_MAP_draft_v1.pdf (annotated)

Can we get a revised proposal by Aug 9 so legal can start redlines?

Regards,
Elena

From: markus.klein@redwood.com <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@novagrid.ai>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Final MAP proposal + DocuSign next steps

Elena —

Thanks for the detailed feedback and the annotated MAP. We’ve incorporated procurement/FP&A asks into Redwood_MAP_Proposal_v2 (attached) and adjusted the escrow and uplift language per your notes:

- Escrow: 25% held, released in three tranches on objective milestone acceptance. Redwood will support a flagged-balance escrow with our standard escrow_terms.docx attached for legal.

- Milestone metrics: each milestone now has objective SLOs (p95 latency < 220ms, successful inference rate > 99.2%, ramp thresholds as stated on page 3).

- Renewal uplift: +5% cap applies only if both MAP milestone completion and avg monthly spend for months 10–12 >= committed baseline. If only milestones are met but spend is < baseline, cap is +10%. Failure to meet milestone thresholds leaves uplift open to negotiation (we’ve capped automatic increases at +15% to avoid runaway pricing).

Next steps:
1) I’ve uploaded the proposal to DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/12345/novagrid-map-proposal (link) — please confirm signers and I’ll route.
2) If legal has redlines, we can accept tracked changes in the DocuSign package or via shared Drive link.
3) On execution, Redwood will schedule a 30-day onboarding check and provide an updated ramp forecast to your engineering team.

Attachments: redwood_map_proposal_v2.pdf, escrow_terms.docx

If this looks good I’ll route for signature today.

Best regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
